nodes.question: Why is there a lack of extensive research on MPs in mangroves compared to plastic waste?
nodes.answer: Most studies have focused primarily on plastic waste, while research on microplastics in mangroves is still in its infancy.
nodes.paragraph: Rivers, surface runoff, and sewage systems indirectly transport MPs, influencing mangrove ecosystems (Mehmood et al. 2023). Wind-driven deposition on beaches and proxim- ity to waste disposal sites also play a significant role in the deposition of MPs in coastal areas (Riaz et al. 2024). Mangrove ecosystems have been found to have substan- tially higher MP contamination as compared to other eco - systems (Liu et al. 2022). Plastic presence in mangrove eco- systems constitutes a significant portion of overall marine debris, as evidenced by recent studies (Browne et al. 2007; Li et al. 2021). Regardless, most studies focus on plastic waste (Browne et al. 2007), while studies on MPs in man- groves are still in their infancy. Previous research found that the mangrove sediment had a higher concentration of MPs compared to the marine sediment in the Beibu Gulf, China. That means the difference was substantially high: 264 2 items/kg in mangrove sediment compared to 0 11 1 items/ kg in marine sediments (Jiao et al. 2021).

nodes.question: What is the primary objective of the study conducted by Ricky et al.?
nodes.answer: The primary objective of the study is to evaluate the impacts of DEET on the biochemical composition of Chlorella vulgaris post-treatment, in order to understand the phycoremediation potential of the algal species relative to its tolerance limit.
nodes.paragraph: This study evaluates the impacts of DEET on the biochemical composition of Chlorella vulgaris post-treatment to understand the phy - coremediation potential of the algal species relative to its tolerance limit. Ricky et al. Environmental Sciences Europe (2025) 37:36 Materials and methods Preparation of DEET stock solution N,N-Diethyl-m-toluamide (DEET) (CAS No: 134-62-3) stock solution (1000 mg/L) was prepared by dissolving 0.1 mL of DEET in 100 mL ultrapure water, and the pH of the stock solution was in the range of 6.9 7.0 consist - ent with the pH of ultrapure water. Working standards required for the test conditions were prepared by serial dilution of the stock solution and kept below 4 C in a dark, enclosed environment. The HPLC eluent prepara - tions employed acetonitrile of HPLC grade. Algae culture incubation conditions and batch experimentation Chlorella vulgaris (BDU GD003) seed cultures were pro - cured from the National Repository for Microalgae and Cyanobacteria-Freshwater, Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu, India. The algae were sub-cultured for 21 days in an orbital shaking incubator to attain stationary phase from seed culture with a fluorescent light intensity of 2000 Ix (12 h light/12 h dark cycle), and the culture was sub-cul - tured in BG-11 medium at 30 C. The experimental setup conditions were identical to prior investigations [23].
